title: Wire bundled-only production data and add component/integration tests
description: Remove the remaining runtime dependency on any first-party API/bootstrap/staging service. For this release, all app-owned informational content is bundled production content and the supplied On The Hook schedule JSON is the authoritative bundled production schedule snapshot. Wire Home, Find Us, Event Detail, Menu, About, More, and Contact through production repositories that resolve entirely from bundled assets/data. Then add component/integration tests against those exact production providers. Do not require or attempt a remote API, staging service, website scrape, WebView extraction, or server push.
acceptance_criteria:
- Copy the supplied schedule snapshot into the app's production content/resources and load it through the production ScheduleRepository.
- The bundled schedule contains 71 events across 17 states with a published window of 2026-08-13 through 2026-08-15.
- Release configuration has no required API base URL, bootstrap endpoint, menu endpoint, about endpoint, schedule endpoint, or staging endpoint.
- Home, Menu, About, More, and Contact render entirely from bundled production content with networking disabled.
- Find Us and Event Detail render from the supplied bundled schedule JSON with networking disabled.
- Search, state/date filtering, sorting, event selection, directions-by-address, and add-to-calendar work from bundled schedule fields.
- Current schedule data contains only actionsAvailable.orderNow, not an order URL. Do not invent an order URL. Render an Order action only when an explicit safe URL is present in production data/config; otherwise omit/disable it cleanly.
- Development/test fixtures remain separate and cannot be selected by a release build.
- Remove tests that require remote override, remote fallback, staging data, or simulated backend responses.
- Component/integration tests exercise the release-selected bundled providers, including Home, Find Us, Menu, About, More, Contact, Event Detail, empty/filter states, and local notification onboarding.
- No runtime HTML scraping or first-party backend is needed to pass this bead.
notes: This bead is the implementation correction that makes the app backend-free. The supplied schedule JSON is a time-bounded production snapshot, not a live feed. Schedule freshness after 2026-08-15 requires replacing the bundled JSON and rebuilding/releasing the app; do not hide that limitation behind fake networking.

title: Add backend-free iOS critical-flow E2E tests
description: Implement critical-flow E2E coverage against the exact release configuration: bundled production informational content plus the bundled 71-event schedule snapshot. No API server, staging server, mock HTTP server, remote bootstrap, or server-driven push infrastructure may be required for the suite.
acceptance_criteria:
- Launch the release-like app on iOS with no first-party backend configured.
- Home -> Find Us -> search/filter -> Event Detail passes using the bundled schedule snapshot.
- A known bundled event such as West Des Moines, IA on 2026-08-15 can be located and opened.
- Location denied -> manual city/state search works without network-backed app data.
- Menu, About, More, and Contact paths pass with networking disabled.
- Directions test asserts handoff to the OS maps mechanism using the event address; it does not require an OTH backend.
- Add-to-calendar works from bundled event date/hours/address.
- Order action is absent/disabled when no explicit order URL exists; tests must not infer one from actionsAvailable.orderNow.
- Notification onboarding and any scheduled reminders are local-device behaviors only; no live push delivery is required.
- Critical suite passes on both iOS without starting any backend/staging/mock HTTP service.
notes: Use deterministic bundled production data, not 'staging' or 'remote substitute' terminology.

title: Execute final backend-free acceptance and signoff
description: Perform final acceptance against the concrete release architecture: bundled production content plus the supplied bundled schedule snapshot. A backend, bootstrap API, menu/about API, schedule API, staging service, mock HTTP server, or server-driven push service must not be required for signoff.
acceptance_criteria:
- All remaining open child beads are closed or explicitly waived for a reason unrelated to an absent backend.
- Release-like iOS builds launch with no first-party API/backend configuration.
- Home, Menu, About, More, and Contact pass using bundled production content only.
- Find Us and Event Detail pass using the supplied 71-event schedule snapshot only.
- Manual search/filtering works, including a known event in the snapshot.
- Directions and add-to-calendar work from bundled event data.
- Order is not fabricated from the orderNow boolean; it is only available when an explicit safe URL exists.
- Local notification onboarding/reminder behavior passes without APNs/FCM server delivery.
- Development fixtures, staging providers, and mock HTTP data cannot be activated by release configuration.
- No runtime website scraping, native cart/checkout, or hidden dependency on private OTH infrastructure exists.
- Acceptance report explicitly records the schedule snapshot window (2026-08-13 through 2026-08-15) and the need to replace/rebuild for fresher schedules.
notes: Absence of any backend/API is expected and must not be treated as a blocker.

title: Document the backend-free bundled-content release model
description: Document how to build, run, test, and update the app with no first-party backend. Explain the bundled production content model, the supplied schedule snapshot, how to replace that schedule for a future build, native maps/calendar handoffs, local notification behavior, and the strict separation between production bundled content and test fixtures.
acceptance_criteria:
- README states plainly that no OTH backend/API is required for this release.
- Document the production bundled content locations for Home/Menu/About/More/Contact and schedule data.
- Document that the current schedule snapshot has 71 events across 17 states covering 2026-08-13 through 2026-08-15.
- Document the exact procedure for replacing/validating the bundled schedule JSON before a future release.
- Document that schedule data is a snapshot and will not self-update without a future data-delivery mechanism.
- Document that local notifications can only be scheduled from data already present on the device.
- Document directions and calendar integration without requiring backend services.
- Document that Order is shown only when an explicit safe order URL exists; actionsAvailable.orderNow alone is insufficient.
- Remove setup instructions that imply a required API base URL, bootstrap service, staging service, or backend server.
- Development fixtures are clearly marked test/dev-only and cannot be selected in release configuration.
notes: This documentation should make a fresh clone runnable and testable without access to any private OTH infrastructure.

title: Run backend-free release privacy and store-readiness review
description: Review the actual backend-free release configuration for Apple/Google readiness. The app ships with bundled production content and a bundled schedule snapshot, uses native device capabilities where needed, and has no required first-party API or server-driven push service.
acceptance_criteria:
- Release build starts and exposes its core informational/navigation experience without a first-party backend.
- Privacy disclosures match actual use of foreground location, calendar, notifications, and external link handoffs.
- App does not request background location unless a separately implemented, justified feature requires it; current release should not.
- No claim of live schedule updates is made because the schedule is bundled snapshot data.
- No claim of server-driven real-time notifications is made; current reminders are local-device only.
- Release build cannot select development fixtures or staging/mock HTTP providers.
- Official logo/icon/splash assets are present.
- Ordering remains external and is only exposed when an explicit safe URL exists in production data/config.
- Store screenshots/metadata do not imply capabilities that require an unavailable backend.
notes: There are no backend-dependent capabilities to waive for this release; they are simply out of scope.
